title: One flamethrower to end them all
author: Poptocrack
selftext:
Should I publish this on Steam ?

Burn the Haystack, start with a flamethrower.

Estimated lenght of game: 30s

Made with Opus 5.5, blender, Rust and Bevy

comments.author: Dependent-Review-727
comments.body: does it use the GPU or just optimized CPU computing? how well does it perform?

replies.author: Poptocrack
replies.body:
All GPU! It's Rust + Bevy, with the simulation written as wgpu compute shaders (ported from a WebGPU prototype I made first).

It runs at a smooth 60 fps for now, without much optimization, I need to push this further if I intend to release it.

replies.author: Dependent-Review-727
replies.body:
what hardware did you test it on? What's the FPS without vsync/frame limiting? How much individual haystacks there are? Do they have any behaviour beyond flame collision and falling? How much did you have to guide the AI to implement it?

also how much time did you spend on it? If it can output 60 FPS on like 3060 with idk, like 500k-1mil hay needles, that's quite impressive

replies.author: Poptocrack
replies.body:
M1 Pro MacBook, no 3060 test yet. Uncapped it's 50-60 fps at 1080p with 1M straws, the sim is cheap, most of the cost is rendering. Haystacks start at 1M straws and grow each round.  
  
Straws rest on each other through a density grid, so burning one spot makes the stack cave in; heat spreads, the needle heats up and the magnet can't feel it above 770 °C. Built with

Claude Code, I did the design, prototype and direction. About 2 days.  
Started with a GDD and a Visual directions document before any code.
